# Original detection stings and recorded pursuit bed

The requested reference is the strong recognition/escape pressure of a horror
game. No audio, melody, asset or soundtrack from that game was copied. The
composition uses licensed independent physical contacts, human performances and
acoustic instrument samples. All preparation and validation ran without speaker
playback; candidate comparison uses provenance, duration, source energy and
available performance texture, not an undocumented claim of human listening.

Two retained CC0 violin candidates were selected from their creators' pages:
cms4f's **Violin scratch.wav**, explicitly described as an acoustic recording,
and ldk1609's **violin tremolo F3.aif** instrument sample. The scratch provides
abrasive bowed detail and the sustained tremolo supplies a tonal rapid-string
bed. Scratch-only would become a continuous scrape; tremolo-only would leave
little percussive urgency. The final bed uses both with the project's already
retained real plank and ratchet recordings. Both original public high-quality
MP3 previews are retained honestly as MP3 previews, not lossless WAV originals.

The two stings compare a metal-led immediate attack against a plank/bow-led
attack with a shortened real human scream. The first includes OwlishMedia's
frightened breath; the second retains a distinct human scream start plus breath.
These sources and bart's physical wood/metal workshop originals were already
retained and credited. The new cues remain separate from recognition and actor
voices: 1.06/1.12 seconds, peak .50/.52, with an immediate attack and a decaying
tail. There is no pre-roll wait or generic synthetic replacement.

The pursuit composition is **150 BPM, 16 beats, 6.4 seconds**, with the real
string sample at two close rate changes, acoustic bow rasp, physical plank
percussion and off-beat ratchet articulation. It contains no extra heartbeat;
the existing real heartbeat keeps that role. Each sustained string layer uses
a .4-second tail/head overlap without fading the whole loop to silence, while
actual percussion tails wrap across the bar. The prepared peak is .32 and the
suggested runtime source maximum gain is .22, leaving headroom for monster
contacts, recognition and the existing mix. Actual engine gain/ducking, onset,
release, spatial ownership and comfort settings belong to the runtime owner.

Rebuild offline with `SourceArt/Audio/render_detection_pursuit.py` and the pinned
`requirements-corridor.txt`. The renderer verifies every original hash, preserves
Unity GUIDs, and updates the canonical manifest and prepared-cues record. Run
`Tools/quality/verify_recorded_audio.py` for inventory/original/PCM/loop-boundary
checks. These checks do not certify human listening quality, imported Unity
mixing, device output or pause/mute behavior; engine diagnostics use the explicit
current-process silence guard before retaining native pre-device DSP.
